goal: Determine whether and how a generic Ontological Way Clear model can provide reason-complete, evidence-bound readiness across definitions, criteria, requirements, Definitions of Done, architecture, designs, and UX plans without collapsing their distinct meanings, owners, evidence classes, or lifecycle gates.
context: The current public Way Clear experiment deterministically blocks only on decision nodes preclassified as open or fog; it does not validate evidence, type the remaining reasons deeply, or establish a reusable ontology. The requested research must compare local definitions, ontology, readiness, architecture, design, and UX precedents with current formal semantics, requirements and architecture standards, and human-centered evidence practice. The target is a candidate ontology plus closure-query contract and finite witness corpus, not implementation, canonical definition, ontology promotion, public extraction, release, or production readiness. All results remain private under cyberAlchemy-v2 until a separate owner-routed decision accepts any reusable generic slice.
anti_bias_global: Formal semantic closure versus lifecycle-operational sufficiency versus context-sensitive architecture and human-evidence honesty, followed by precedent, non-vacuity, and definitional non-collapse attacks.

groups.anti_bias: Composite methodology and source-corpus axis: formal ontology and constraint semantics, lifecycle and acceptance standards, and architecture/design/UX evidence practice.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs formal ontology, open-world semantics, constraints, provenance, and closure logic while agent 1 runs requirements, acceptance, Definition-of-Done, verification, and lifecycle standards on the methodology and source-corpus axis; a bias in agent 0 toward logically elegant but operationally indeterminate closure would be exposed by agent 1, while a bias in agent 1 toward process checklists without semantic identity would be exposed by agent 0.

Agent 0 runs formal artifact and relation semantics while agent 2 runs architecture, design-rationale, UX-plan, accessibility, and human-evidence analysis on the methodology and source-corpus axis; a bias in agent 0 toward universal decidable closure would be exposed by agent 2 where design and UX retain contextual or human-study residue, while a bias in agent 2 toward irreducible context would be exposed by agent 0 where exact dependencies and obligations are machine-checkable.

Agent 1 runs lifecycle admission and acceptance-evidence analysis while agent 2 runs architecture/design/UX intent, rationale, usability, and human-evidence analysis on the methodology and source-corpus axis; a bias in agent 1 toward binary completion would be exposed by agent 2 when deterministic proxies cannot establish comprehension or preference, while a bias in agent 2 toward perpetual qualitative openness would be exposed by agent 1 where an owner-approved bounded transition has explicit evidence.

agents.angle: Formal ontology and semantics: model artifact kinds, normative statements, obligations, evidence, dependencies, contradictions, scope closure, provenance, epistemic state, and query semantics under explicit open-world and declared-closed-world assumptions.
agents.initial_prompt: Research the formal-semantic lane for Ontological Way Clear. Start from the live public Way Clear experiment and the selected Inventory leads, then verify current primary technical sources such as official W3C RDF/OWL/SHACL/PROV specifications and relevant primary formal-methods papers. Determine which shared primitives and relations can span Definition, Criterion, Requirement, DefinitionOfDone, Architecture, Design, and UXPlan without making those artifact kinds identical. Address open-world versus closed-world validation, local completeness declarations, monotonic and non-monotonic change, contradiction, unknown/fog, stale evidence, provenance, authority, named closure profiles, bounded closure queries, reason completeness, and deterministic receipts. Return exact local selectors and external citations, a candidate type/relation table, state and reason-code algebra, invariants, countermodels, and unresolved formal limits. Treat Inventory as discovery only; do not edit or promote any artifact. Budget about 5000 tokens.

agents.angle: Lifecycle and acceptance semantics: distinguish definitions, criteria, requirements, acceptance conditions, Definitions of Done, verification evidence, readiness projections, owner decisions, and transition-specific closure profiles.
agents.initial_prompt: Research the lifecycle and acceptance lane for Ontological Way Clear. Verify current local Definitions Governance, Work Pack Readiness, Task Session, ontology-lifecycle, and requirement/acceptance precedents surfaced by the Inventory packet, plus current primary sources from official ISO/IEC/IEEE requirements and architecture standards, the official Scrum Guide for Definition of Done, and primary assurance/traceability literature where accessible. Classify what makes a definition usable, a criterion decidable, a requirement acceptable, a DoD satisfiable without circular self-assertion, and a transition ready. Separate artifact quality, evidence sufficiency, owner approval, execution completion, promotion, and release. Return exact citations, artifact-kind closure obligations, relation and owner mappings, stale/invalidation behavior, evidence classes, false-clear cases, and what must remain profile-local rather than universal. Do not convert paywalled abstracts or Inventory summaries into verified content. Do not edit files. Budget about 5000 tokens.

agents.angle: Architecture, design, and UX evidence: model viewpoints, decisions, rationale, concerns, alternatives, traceability, validation plans, accessibility and usability evidence, and the boundary between deterministic proxies and human findings.
agents.initial_prompt: Research the architecture/design/UX lane for Ontological Way Clear. Inspect the live OEW focus-scene architecture and the selected UX/readiness Inventory leads, then verify current primary sources such as official ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 material, official ISO human-centred-design sources where accessible, W3C WCAG documentation, and primary design-rationale or UX-evidence research. Determine which obligations can be machine-closed and which require named owner judgment, human study, screenshot review, or explicit residue. Distinguish Architecture from Design and UXPlan while tracing requirements, concerns, viewpoints, decisions, alternatives, risks, prototypes, research questions, measures, accessibility assertions, and human-evidence ceilings. Return exact citations, kind-specific closure profiles, cross-artifact relations, deterministic versus human evidence classes, negative examples, and portability limits. Do not infer ontology membership from presentation grouping and do not edit files. Budget about 5000 tokens.

Reconcile the three explorer returns into one exact-bound Ontological Way Clear candidate without erasing their disagreements. Partition shared substrate from artifact-kind ClosureProfiles. At minimum evaluate Artifact, ArtifactKind, StatementKind, Obligation, Decision, Claim, Evidence, EvidenceClass, Owner, AuthorityEffect, LifecycleState, ScopeDeclaration, Dependency, Refines, Satisfies, Covers, ConflictsWith, BlockedBy, VerifiedBy, InvalidatedBy, ClosureProfile, ClosureQuery, ReasonCode, and WayClearReceipt. Define whether clear means artifact-internally coherent, transition-admissible, or both; never collapse those gates. Produce seven kind profiles for Definition, Criterion, Requirement, DefinitionOfDone, Architecture, Design, and UXPlan; a cross-artifact dependency DAG; open/fog/closed/stale/superseded/out-of-scope semantics; version and digest rules; reason-complete output; and a finite fixture matrix with at least one positive chain plus false-clear and false-block mutants for every kind. Every load-bearing row must carry immutable source identity, exact selector or structured pointer, explorer-return reference, evidence scope, and observed/executed/unverified status. Mark build-from-owned, proposal, deferred, and killed candidates distinctly. Return an evidence-closure candidate matrix; do not write repository files. Budget about 7000 tokens.

groups.anti_bias: Attack-vector axis: precedent ownership, non-vacuity and counter-example execution, and definitional plus scope non-collapse.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs the precedent and owner gate while agent 1 runs finite-witness, mutation, and counter-example pressure on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 0 toward reusing existing validators would be exposed by agent 1 when they cannot change a cross-artifact verdict, while a bias in agent 1 toward new machinery would be exposed by agent 0 when an existing owner already supplies the behavior.

Agent 0 runs precedent and ownership classification while agent 2 runs definitional and scope-collapse attacks on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 0 toward extending one broad owner would be exposed by agent 2 when distinct artifact meanings collapse, while a bias in agent 2 toward proliferating vocabulary would be exposed by agent 0 when an existing term and relation already owns the distinction.

Agent 1 runs executable paper fixtures and false-clear/false-block mutants while agent 2 runs tautology, category-error, and authority-collapse attacks on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 1 toward a passing demo would be exposed by agent 2 when the fixture merely re-labels a checklist, while a bias in agent 2 toward semantic purity would be exposed by agent 1 when a distinct relation produces a necessary observable verdict.

agents.angle: Precedent gate: locate existing local and external owners for every proposed type, relation, closure profile, validator, evidence class, lifecycle state, and receipt before accepting novelty.
agents.initial_prompt: Apply only the precedent gate to the synthesized Ontological Way Clear candidate. Verify the live Way Clear experiment, Definitions Governance, Ontology Vault and lifecycle, Inventory, Work Pack Readiness, Task Session, architecture/design/UX owners, and cited primary external standards or formal methods. Classify each candidate as already-deployed, build-from-owned, or precedent-clean. Find duplicate ontologies, second sources of truth, second lifecycle gates, generic checklists, SHACL/OWL/PROV features, assurance-case concepts, requirements traceability, architecture-conformance, or UX-evidence taxonomies that already own the behavior. Precedent never emits KILL; return exact owners, selectors, missing-source defects, and bounded reuse consequences. Route missing evidence only through the declared synthesizer-to-explorer feedback edge. Budget about 3500 tokens.

agents.angle: Non-vacuity and counter-example gate: force the candidate through a finite seven-artifact dependency graph with positive closure, open/fog, missing evidence, contradiction, staleness, owner-approval, human-study, and scope mutants.
agents.initial_prompt: Apply the non-vacuity gate. Construct the smallest paper-executable graph containing one Definition, Criterion, Requirement, DefinitionOfDone, Architecture, Design, and UXPlan linked by the proposed relations. Require one all-clear case and discriminating mutants for circular definition, criterion without observable, unverifiable requirement, self-certifying DoD, unresolved architecture tension, design without requirement/rationale binding, UX plan without a research question or evidence-class boundary, stale receipt, conflicting owners, out-of-scope node, and open-world unknown. Replay each case deterministically and ask whether the returned reasons are complete and whether evaluation mutates state. KILL any candidate primitive or relation that cannot change an observable verdict, cannot distinguish false-clear from false-block, or merely restates an owner checklist without computable value. Return witness tables, expected receipts, KILLs, and gaps. Budget about 4000 tokens.

agents.angle: Definitional and scope gate: attack collapse among artifact kind, statement kind, obligation, evidence, decision, owner approval, lifecycle state, computed readiness, completion, promotion, and authority.
agents.initial_prompt: Apply the definitional-soundness gate to the synthesis. Test whether Ontological Way Clear is a real relation/query model or a renamed readiness checklist; whether one governed Artifact supertype erases Definition, Criterion, Requirement, DoD, Architecture, Design, and UXPlan meanings; whether unknown, fog, open, invalid, stale, blocked, and incomplete are distinguishable; and whether evidence validity, artifact quality, transition admission, execution completion, promotion, publication, and production readiness remain separate. Require each surviving type and relation to have a distinct owner, invariant, failure mode, and evidence artifact. Return KEEP/MERGE/RENAME/DEFER/KILL with citations and a smallest repaired vocabulary. KILL tautological or definitionally collapsed candidates only; do not edit files. Budget about 3500 tokens.

Write findings.md only from the evidence-closed synthesis and reviewer receipts. Lead with whether Ontological Way Clear survives and under what name and authority ceiling. Include: existing-owner and precedent map; shared ontology substrate; seven artifact-kind ClosureProfiles; relation vocabulary; state/reason algebra; bounded open-world/closed-world policy; evidence and authority boundaries; cross-artifact dependency DAG; closure-query and receipt contract; finite positive and mutant fixture matrix; migration path from the current open/fog predicate; blind spots and typed residue; and the required verdict matrix. Every load-bearing claim cites explorer evidence and exact selectors, and every candidate is labeled observed, executed, build-from-owned, proposed, deferred, or killed. Do not write research.md or modify Arcanum, ontology, definitions, product, generated, Inventory, ledger, Git, publication, or release surfaces. Budget about 7000 tokens.

Audit findings.md only against the frozen goal and exact-binding contract. Require complete coverage of all seven artifact families, current local selectors, primary external sources, a non-vacuous positive and mutant corpus, explicit open-world versus closure-scope semantics, reason completeness, staleness/invalidation, owner and authority separation, the verdict matrix, and an implementable candidate contract without claiming implementation. Reject if the model collapses artifact kinds, confuses evidence with truth or approval, lets a clear receipt promote anything, uses browser proxies as human comprehension, or claims canonical ontology, public extraction, adoption, release, or production readiness. Return ACCEPT or one bounded writer revision list. Budget about 3500 tokens.
